topic: A neighbor asks to use part of the yard for a garden
text: The boundary between our spaces is often a whimsical line, less about ownership and more about the flow of life and seasons. When the neighbor approached, there was no tension, only a gentle curiosity about the nature of their request. They spoke of planting, of nurturing growth, a shared respect for the land. The idea of part of the yard becoming a garden seemed a natural extension of what already exists here, a blending of efforts rather than a division. There was no rush, no urgency to decide; instead, the conversation felt like the slow unfolding of a leaf, each detail coming into light at its own pace. The proposal was met with a nod, a wordless agreement that some things need not be defined by limits but by the mutual care we bring to them.
